deities: The Formless Divine, worshipped through the Holy Name (Naam) - no idols in the Ekasarana tradition

history.period: Establishment date disputed: 1461 CE vs 1528 CE (flag)
history.summary: Not a conventional idol temple but a Bor Naamghar (large congregational prayer hall) of the Ekasarana Dharma, founded by saint-reformer Madhavdeva at Dhekiakhowa village, 15 km east of Jorhat town and 3.5 km off NH-37 (CSV town 'Jorhat' corrected to the actual village). Legend: Madhavdeva, hosted by a poor old woman who could offer only rice with dhekia saak (fiddlehead fern), founded the namghar here - hence 'Dhekiakhowa' (eating dhekia). He lit an earthen lamp (akhanda banti) that the managing committee says has burned continuously since 1528 (1450 Saka), refueled with mustard oil by priests. It is called a Bornamghar for its large campus and historical association. Date conflict flagged: most sources give establishment as 1461 CE with the lamp lit in 1528, while some give 1528 for both; one source also misattributes the founding to Srimanta Sankardeva himself. The complex spans ~13 bighas and includes the main hall, Monikut, and a holy pond (sarovar).

name: Dhekiakhowa Bornamghar
town_description: Dhekiakhowa is a village in Jorhat district of Upper Assam, about 15 km east of Jorhat town just off National Highway 37. It sits amid the tea gardens and paddy fields of the Brahmaputra valley and is known almost entirely for its famous Bornamghar, one of the most revered Neo-Vaishnavite prayer halls in Assam.

travel.airport: Rowriah (Jorhat) Airport (~15 km west) is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Jorhat Town Railway Station (~15 km) is the nearest major railway station.
travel.road: 15 km east of Jorhat town, 3.5 km off National Highway 37; reachable by taxi or auto-rickshaw from Jorhat.

visitor_information.best_time: The Assamese month of Bhado/Bhadra (mid-August to mid-September) for Naam-Proxongo; open all year.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily; free entry (per travelsetu.com - verify locally).
